request: Replace mobile thumb stick with left and right arrows; hide arrows in tilt mode; retain other controls.
changes: Two independent, holdable SVG arrow buttons with accessible labels and pressed feedback.
Opposite arrows cancel, and releasing either restores the remaining held direction. Pointer capture, keyboard ownership and blur/menu resets release correctly.
Tilt hides only the steering group after motion access succeeds. Pending, denied, rejected or unsupported access retains arrow controls.
Out-of-order permission results cannot change a newer mode. Saved settings and visible selection revert consistently on permission failure.
Startup defers iOS motion permission until a user gesture; the legacy saved mode ID remains compatible.
Steering labels/help updated; GO, BRAKE, FLY and ACT preserved.
An open menu remains usable before portrait rotation guidance appears.

validation.result: PASS: TypeScript, ten regression suites, production build; UI suite expanded to20 groups.
validation.legacyTool: node --check tools/userplay.mjs passed after updating its arrow selectors; it was not run as a playtest.

browser.environment: Chrome native DevTools mobile emulation; visible controls only; no hidden game-state mutation or autopilot.
completed: Loaded area and accepted a test order to expose controls.
Focused left and right arrow buttons held with Space plus W throttle, then released and braked.
Enabled Tilt the phone in Settings: arrows disappeared; GO/BRAKE/FLY/ACT stayed visible.
Switched to Arrow buttons: both arrows returned.
Measured landscape targets60x64,portrait50x64;8px gaps and no overlap with pedals at320px width.
limitations: This was device emulation, not physical phone motion. Permission denial, multi-pointer ownership and sensor values were exercised in offline production-code regressions.
Pointer dispatch in device emulation timed out on the first Play attempt; visible buttons were subsequently activated with focused keyboard controls.
